workflows.pain_point: Developers spend significant manual effort writing unit and regression tests after completing features, especially for older services
workflows.current_process: Developer finishes a feature and then manually writes unit and regression tests
workflows.frequency: Every sprint, sometimes more frequently when dealing with production bugs or larger releases
workflows.evidence: Alex: 'For some of the payments services, I'll finish a feature and then spend another couple of hours writing the unit and regression tests.' Mark: 'Testing is probably the biggest one for my team. Developers still spend a lot of time writing and updating tests manually, especially when we make changes to older services.'

workflows.pain_point: When codebase changes, developers must manually determine which existing tests are still relevant and add new ones, involving repetitive work
workflows.current_process: Developers figure out which existing tests are still relevant when something changes in the codebase and add new tests as needed
workflows.evidence: Mark: 'And it's not just writing the tests. When something changes in the codebase, we have to figure out which existing tests are still relevant and add new ones. A lot of that work is repetitive.'

workflows.pain_point: Senior engineers spend time reviewing tests created by junior developers rather than writing tests themselves
workflows.current_process: Senior engineers review tests created by junior developers
workflows.evidence: Mark: 'I'd estimate two to three hours per developer per sprint, although the senior engineers probably spend less time writing the tests themselves and more time reviewing what the junior developers create.'

organizational_context.current_ai_adoption: Team is using AI tool for basic code completion and boilerplate work
organizational_context.adoption_stage: Early adoption - have not changed how the engineering organization works yet
organizational_context.decision_maker_priority: Reducing manual effort in testing workflows while maintaining quality
organizational_context.pilot_readiness: Ready for small pilot with payments team using developers already using the AI tool regularly
key_concerns: Generated tests may look correct but miss important edge cases
Need to keep engineers in the loop and require developer review before merging
Risk of developers blindly accepting AI-generated output
Need evidence of time saved, quality maintained, and actual usage before broad rollout

workflows.pain_point: Engineers spend an hour or more figuring out what legacy code does before making changes, especially in older services written years ago that are no longer well understood
workflows.current_process: Search through repository, review old documentation, check Jira tickets, and ask colleagues who previously worked on the service
workflows.frequency: Several times a week across the team
workflows.evidence: Neha: 'When I get assigned an issue in one of the older Java services, I can spend an hour or more just figuring out what the code is doing before I can make a change.' Neha: 'Almost every time someone works on one of the older services. Maybe several times a week across the team.'

workflows.pain_point: Even experienced engineers must trace through several services to understand dependency chains
workflows.evidence: Michael: 'Even experienced engineers sometimes have to trace through several services before they understand the dependency chain.'

workflows.pain_point: Information is spread across multiple systems (GitHub, Confluence, Jira, internal documents) making it difficult to locate relevant information
workflows.current_process: Search across GitHub, Confluence, Jira, and internal documents
workflows.evidence: Michael: 'We also have information spread across GitHub, Confluence, Jira, and internal documents. Finding the right information is probably half the problem.'

organizational_context.decision_maker_priority: Reducing time engineers spend understanding legacy code and existing services
organizational_context.pilot_readiness: Ready to pilot with a small engineering group
key_concerns: AI must provide accurate answers grounded in actual code and documentation, not confident but incorrect explanations
Engineers need to see source references and understand where answers came from to build trust
Black-box answers without transparency will not be trusted by engineers
Existing documentation is unreliable and outdated

workflows.pain_point: Senior engineers spend significant time on routine code reviews, creating bottlenecks and preventing focus on architectural changes
workflows.current_process: All pull requests go through GitHub where one or two senior developers review, leave comments, developer makes changes, then PR returns for another review. Automated linting and static analysis are used but don't understand context of changes
workflows.frequency: High volume, particularly for smaller PRs
workflows.evidence: James: 'Code reviews are probably one of the bigger time sinks.' Rahul: 'we also get a lot of repetitive changes where I'm basically checking the same things over and over.' Ananya: 'The problem is that our senior developers are becoming a bottleneck. They need to review the important architectural changes, but they also spend a lot of time on routine reviews.'

organizational_context.current_ai_adoption: Using automated linting and static analysis tools, but not AI-assisted solutions
organizational_context.adoption_stage: Early exploration - open to piloting AI-assisted code review
organizational_context.decision_maker_priority: Reducing senior engineer bottleneck while maintaining quality and human oversight of engineering reviews
organizational_context.pilot_readiness: High - clear success metrics identified and willingness to pilot with appropriate guardrails
key_concerns: AI should assist rather than replace human engineering review
AI must provide explanatory context for flagged issues to avoid being ignored
Need to measure actual impact on review time and senior engineer workload
Must track acceptance rate of AI suggestions to validate usefulness

workflows.pain_point: Information is spread across several systems requiring manual gathering of context from logs, dashboards, deployments, Jira tickets, and previous incident reports before troubleshooting can begin
workflows.current_process: Engineers manually look through logs, dashboards, recent deployments, Jira tickets, and previous incident reports to gather context before starting troubleshooting
workflows.frequency: Several incidents every week across services
workflows.evidence: Kevin: 'A lot of the investigation is manual. We look through logs, dashboards, recent deployments, Jira tickets, and previous incident reports.' Arjun: 'An engineer might spend 30 or 40 minutes just gathering context before they start troubleshooting.' Kevin: 'We have several incidents every week across our services.'

workflows.workflow: Gathering incident context for unfamiliar services

workflows.current_process: Engineers manually research service architecture and changes when investigating unfamiliar services
workflows.evidence: Lisa: 'The bigger problem is when the person investigating hasn't seen the service before. They need to understand the architecture and then figure out what changed.'

workflows.pain_point: Engineers don't always know which runbook applies to the incident they are investigating
workflows.current_process: Runbooks exist but are not always followed because engineers don't know which one applies
workflows.evidence: Kevin: 'We have runbooks, but they're not always followed because engineers don't always know which runbook applies to the incident.'

workflows.pain_point: Engineers don't always know where to look in years of incident history to find similar past incidents
workflows.current_process: Manual search through incident history when engineers remember or discover similar incidents may exist
workflows.evidence: Kevin: 'It would also be useful if it could identify similar incidents we've had before. We have years of incident history but engineers don't always know where to look.'

organizational_context.current_ai_adoption: Considering AI for incident investigation but no current implementation mentioned
organizational_context.decision_maker_priority: Reduce investigation time without increasing operational risk
organizational_context.pilot_readiness: High - specific pilot metrics and scope already defined
key_concerns: AI systems must not automatically change production systems
Humans need to remain responsible for final decisions
Need to measure usefulness of AI recommendations and how often engineers discard them
Operational risk must not increase

workflows.pain_point: Documentation is often outdated and doesn't match actual implementation in code, requiring developers to search multiple systems and ask colleagues
workflows.current_process: Search Confluence, GitHub, Jira, and Slack; if answer not found, ask someone on the team who might know

workflows.evidence: Maria: 'We have talked about improving our documentation process, but keeping everything synchronized manually hasn't worked very well.' Daniel: 'It could also help generate documentation when a developer changes an API or introduces a new service.'

organizational_context.current_ai_adoption: Exploring AI solutions for documentation management
organizational_context.decision_maker_priority: Reduce outdated documentation and make it easier for developers to find accurate information
organizational_context.pilot_readiness: Ready to pilot with one service where documentation is particularly problematic
key_concerns: AI-generated documentation must be reviewed by humans before being published
Need to measure baseline metrics before implementation
Want to track success through developer search effectiveness and documentation update speed

Engineering review required before publishing

workflows.pain_point: Engineers spend significant time understanding ticket context by reading Jira comments, related tickets, and searching for missing information before they can estimate or begin work
workflows.current_process: Engineers manually review Jira tickets, read comments, examine related tickets, search through previous tickets and Slack conversations, and schedule meetings with product managers when clarity is still lacking

organizational_context.decision_maker_priority: Reducing time spent in requirement refinement and minimizing clarification cycles between engineering and product
key_concerns: Engineers must be able to verify sources of AI-generated analysis
Solution should not become another system requiring maintenance
Need to measure time spent in refinement, number of clarification cycles, and tickets returned to product

workflows.pain_point: New engineers need to learn architecture, services, development process, and internal tools, but documentation is spread across multiple systems and doesn't always explain how everything fits together

workflows.pain_point: Documentation is spread across multiple platforms (Confluence, GitHub, internal wikis) and finding specific answers takes much longer than asking an experienced engineer

organizational_context.decision_maker_priority: Reducing time to productivity for new engineers and reducing mentoring burden on experienced engineers
